'''Bensonhurst Park''' is a park in [[Bath Beach, Brooklyn|Bath Beach]], [[Brooklyn]], [[New York City]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nycgovparks.org/parks/bensonhurst-park|title=Bensonhurst Park|publisher=New York City Department of Parks and Recreation|language=en|access-date=August 10, 2017}}</ref> The park stretches from the north border at [[Cropsey Avenue]] to the south border at [[Gravesend Bay]]. The park has a playground on the north-east side,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nycgovparks.org/parks/bensonhurst-park/facilities/playgrounds|title=Bensonhurst Park Playgrounds|publisher=New York City Department of Parks and Recreation|language=en|access-date=August 10, 2017}}</ref> a field in the middle of the playground and several basketball courts on the west side.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nycgovparks.org/parks/bensonhurst-park/facilities/basketball|title=Bensonhurst Park Basketball Courts|publisher=New York City Department of Parks and Recreation|language=en|access-date=August 10, 2017}}</ref> There is also a bathroom in the northwest side of the park.

==History==
The first calls for a park at Bath Beach began in 1891. The initial 16 acres of parkland was acquired in 1895, followed by additional purchases in 1924 and 1944.<ref>{{Cite web |url = https://www.nycgovparks.org/parks/bensonhurst-park/history |title = Bensonhurst Park Highlights |publisher = New York City Department of Parks and Recreation |language = en |access-date = August 10, 2017 }}</ref>

In 2016, a $6.5 million renovation was announced for Bensonhurst Park.<ref>{{cite news |url = https://bklyner.com/gentile-secures-6-million-renovation-bensonhurst-park-bensonhurst |title = EXCLUSIVE: $6.5 Million In Renovations Coming To Bensonhurst Park |newspaper = [[BKLYNER]] |first = Rachel |last = Silberstein | date = August 12, 2016 |access-date = June 3, 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last = Caramanno |first = Thomas |url = http://brooklynink.org/2016/09/12/55056-bensonhurst-park-is-about-to-get-a-makeover |title = Bensonhurst Park Is About To Get A Makeover |work = The Brooklyn Ink |date = 2016-09-12 |access-date = June 3, 2019 }}</ref> Renovations began in September 2019 with an expected completion date.<ref>{{Cite web |url = https://www.nycgovparks.org/planning-and-building/capital-project-tracker/project/7363 |title = Bensonhurst Park Playground Reconstruction |publisher = New York City Department of Parks and Recreation |access-date = June 3, 2019 }}</ref>

The renovations were completed in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bensonhurst Park News - NEW AND IMPROVED: NYC PARKS UNVEILS THE NEWLY RECONSTRUCTED BENSONHURST PARK PLAYGROUND : NYC Parks |url=https://www.nycgovparks.org/parks/bensonhurst-park/pressrelease/21802 |access-date=2025-09-15 |website=www.nycgovparks.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-01-07 |title=Renovated Bensonhurst Playground Opens To Public This Week |url=https://bklyner.com/renovated-bensonhurst-playground-opens-to-public-this-week/ |access-date=2025-09-15 |website=Bklyner |language=en}}</ref>

==Geography==

Bensonhurst Park's area is {{convert|0.789|mi2}}, which also includes the part south of [[Belt Parkway]]. Without the southern part, this park would be only about {{convert|14|acre}}. Bensonhurst Park borders [[Cropsey Avenue]] to the north, [[Belt Parkway]] in the middle, [[Bay Parkway (Brooklyn)|Bay Parkway]] to the east, and 21st Avenue to the west. The park borders [[Gravesend Bay]] as well.
